_comment: Conformance cases for parse_base64_ticket, taken from datrail/gateway's tests/vectors/ticket.json at 6758b77. Headers are padded and carry the claims Rail Center mints, plus unread keys where a case's own bytes are its point. Cases about how the header arrives are the runtime's and are removed, as are cases this parser answers differently from the gateway: all of those are input Rail Center does not mint.

cases.name: not base64 at all
base64 of bytes that are not JSON
two headers joined by a comma, so the caller picks which is read
a JSON array rather than an object
a missing exp is malformed rather than unbounded
a fractional exp
exp true, which is an int in Python and must not read as 1970
shape is checked before expiry, so a stale payload with an unusable exp reports malformed
past its expiry
exactly at its expiry is expired, not valid
an expired ticket surrenders its claims - a stale score is not a basis
one second before expiry is still valid
a complete ticket
carries the nested posture, the alignment and the skills
a padded spelling decodes
a NaN literal is not JSON
an Infinity literal is not JSON
a -Infinity literal is not JSON
invalid UTF-8 inside an otherwise valid JSON string
cases.note: the TypeScript reference substitutes U+FFFD and reaches valid; this refuses bytes it could not read

cases.name: exp null
exp as a string
a JSON scalar rather than an object
the JSON literal null
a stray comma splicing two payloads
shape is checked before expiry - a stale ticket with an unusable exp is malformed
the same payload decodes with its padding
nesting at the cap is still read
a bracket inside a string is a character, not structure
invalid UTF-8 in a key
cases.note: the reference substitutes U+FFFD, so the key is no longer agent_id and it reports malformed; both refuse, on different states

cases.name: a MIME-wrapped header is refused rather than quietly unwrapped
a body one past a multiple of four is undecodable
a doubled byte-order mark leaves a character that is not JSON
cases.note: Exactly one mark is dropped. The second is an ordinary U+FEFF.

cases.name: a byte-order mark anywhere but the start is an ordinary character
an exp at exactly the largest safe integer is still read
an exp at the negative end of the safe range is expired, not malformed
seventy structures opened and closed in turn nest two deep, not seventy-one
cases.note: Pins that the scanner decrements on a close. Counting opens alone reaches seventy-one on a ticket that never nests past its own skills list.

cases.name: an escaped quote does not end the string it is inside
cases.note: Seventy brackets follow an escaped quote. Without escape handling the scanner leaves the string there and reads them as structure, past the cap.

cases.name: the url-safe alphabet decodes
a leading '=' is a corrupted body, not a differently-padded one
cases.note: Padding comes off the end and nowhere else. Stripping every '=' instead would take this one too and hand back a usable ticket.

cases.name: a trailing newline on the header is not trimmed away
a leading space on the header is not trimmed away
a trailing tab on the header is not trimmed away
an exp of zero is expired, not malformed
cases.note: The one value where testing `exp is None` and testing its truth diverge, and the state is what a refusal is eventually reported as.

cases.name: two padded tickets run together read as the first alone
sixty-five sibling objects nest two deep, not sixty-six
cases.note: A closer that counts only ']' never comes back down, so the enclosing object and sixty-five siblings leave it at sixty-six and a ticket that barely nests is refused.

cases.name: exp false is malformed, as exp true is
cases.note: The other half of the boolean rule. abs(False) is zero, so a guard written as `exp is True` reads this as the epoch and reports expired -- a state that says the ticket was once good.

cases.name: a raw control character inside a string is not JSON
cases.note: RFC 8259 requires escaping below U+0020 and JSON.parse refuses it. Python's json refuses it too unless asked not to.

cases.name: a duplicate key takes the last value, as JSON.parse does
cases.note: Unspecified by RFC 8259 and agreed by both runtimes. A first-wins reading would honour an expiry the sender wrote over.

cases.name: a now of zero is an instant, not a missing argument
cases.note: The epoch is a real instant. Testing `now` for truth rather than for None falls back to the wall clock and judges the ticket against a different moment than the caller asked for.

cases.name: a lone surrogate is not UTF-8
cases.note: The contract names this one: a decoder configured to let surrogates through reads the ticket and a strict one refuses it, with every claim in it chosen by whoever sent it. Divergent for the first documented reason: Buffer.toString substitutes U+FFFD and never throws, so the reference admits an agent_id with a replacement character in it.

an agent on no baseline
